name: Bengaluru Tenant Security Deposit Withholding
raw_input: I was renting a 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru for 2 years at Rs 28,000/month. I gave 1 lakh rupees as security deposit. I gave proper 1-month notice on 1st October and vacated the flat on 31st October 2024. I cleared all electricity and water bills and handed over keys. Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the deposit via UPI in 3 days. Now it has been 25 days, he stopped picking my calls, and yesterday he messaged saying he is deducting Rs 45,000 for 'complete house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning'. There was no damage, just normal nail holes for photo frames and standard wear and tear. I have move-in photos, move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, and WhatsApp chat where he acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition. How can I get my Rs 45,000 back?

case_dossier.case_title: Security Deposit Refund Dispute – Unjust Rs 45,000 Deduction
case_dossier.summary: The tenant vacated a 2BHK flat on 31 Oct 2024 after giving proper notice. The landlord promised a full security‑deposit refund but now claims a Rs 45,000 deduction for repainting and cleaning, despite no damage. The tenant seeks the deducted amount back.

timeline.event: Tenant occupied 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru on a 2‑year lease at Rs 28,000 per month, paid Rs 1,00,000 security deposit.
Tenant gave one‑month notice to vacate.
Tenant vacated the flat, cleared electricity & water bills, handed over keys, and landlord acknowledged receipt in good condition via WhatsApp.
Landlord promised to refund the full security deposit via UPI within three days.
No refund received; landlord stopped answering calls.
Landlord messaged that he is deducting Rs 45,000 for repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning.

evidence_held: Bank statements showing monthly rent payments and security‑deposit payment
WhatsApp chat where landlord acknowledges receiving the flat in good condition
Copy of the notice sent on 1 Oct 2024 (if any)
evidence_needed: Signed rent/lease agreement specifying security‑deposit terms and deductions allowed
Receipt or acknowledgment of the Rs 1,00,000 security deposit paid
Written notice of termination (email or WhatsApp screenshot) sent on 1 Oct 2024
Any written communication from landlord detailing the Rs 45,000 deduction (e.g., screenshot of the message, email)
Inventory or condition checklist signed by both parties at move‑in and move‑out (if exists)
Quotes/receipts for repainting, marble polishing, or deep‑cleaning (to verify if deduction is justified)
UPI transaction history showing no refund received
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Strong visual (photos/video) and transactional records plus landlord's acknowledgment, but missing the formal lease clause and written deduction notice.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
You are in a strong position under Indian law to get your full security deposit back. The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (where adopted by Karnataka) caps the security deposit at two months' rent and requires the landlord to return it within 30 days of you handing over peaceful possession, after deducting only genuine, itemised charges. Ordinary wear‑and‑tear – like the natural fading of paint or normal cleaning – cannot be used to keep part of the deposit. The landlord’s claim of a Rs 45,000 deduction for repainting, marble polishing and deep cleaning is not automatically valid, especially because you have video evidence that the flat was handed back in good condition and the landlord himself confirmed receipt.

Because the dispute is about money you are owed, it is a civil matter, not a criminal cheating case. You can first ask the landlord in writing to refund the amount (with interest for delay) and, if he does not comply, you may approach the Rent Authority or a Small Causes Court, which allows you to represent yourself without a lawyer. The evidence you already have – photos, videos, payment records and the WhatsApp acknowledgment – will support your claim that no real damage was caused and that the deduction is unjustified.

governing_laws.relevance: Limits security deposit to 2 months' rent and mandates refund within 30 days after peaceful possession.
Prohibits deduction for normal wear and tear; requires itemised bills for any legitimate deduction.
Specifies that deposit disputes must be filed before the Rent Authority/Rent Court, not a regular civil court.
Tenant must keep the property in as good condition as received, subject only to reasonable wear and tear.
Tenant is entitled to the return of the security deposit after vacating and handing over vacant possession.

governing_laws.act_name: General Legal Principle (Civil vs. Criminal Boundary)
governing_laws.relevance: Refund disputes are civil matters; criminal cheating charges are inappropriate unless fraud was present from the start.

action_options.title: Send Formal Legal Notice to Landlord
action_options.cost_estimate: Free to minimal (Speed Post/Registered Email, approx. Rs. 50‑200)
action_options.details: Draft a concise notice stating: (a) you vacated on 31 Oct 2024, (b) landlord acknowledged good condition, (c) under Model Tenancy Act Sec.13 & Sec.14 he must refund the full Rs 1,00,000 deposit within 30 days, (d) the Rs 45,000 deduction is unjustified, (e) demand refund of Rs 45,000 plus 2% per month interest for delay. Attach copies of photos, handover video, WhatsApp acknowledgment, and payment proof. Send by registered post and email, and keep a copy of the receipt.

action_options.title: File Grievance on State Rent Authority / Online Portal
action_options.cost_estimate: Zero court fees up to Rs. 5 Lakhs (online filing is free)
action_options.details: If the landlord does not respond or refuses to pay, log in to Karnataka's Rent Authority portal (or the National Consumer Helpline 1915 for guidance). Upload the notice, evidence (photos, video, payment slips, WhatsApp chat), and a brief statement of claim. The portal generates a reference number and forwards the complaint to the Rent Authority, which will schedule a hearing.

action_options.title: Petition Before Rent Authority / Small Causes Court
action_options.cost_estimate: Nominal court fee (usually Rs. 500‑1,000 for claims up to Rs. 5 Lakhs)
action_options.details: Prepare a petition citing Model Tenancy Act Sec.13,14,21 and Transfer of Property Act Sec.108. Attach all evidence and a copy of the legal notice. You may appear yourself; the forum allows self‑representation. The authority can order the landlord to refund the deposit with interest and may award a modest penalty for wrongful deduction.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can handle the entire process yourself: drafting the notice, filing the online grievance, and appearing before the Rent Authority or Small Causes Court does not require a lawyer. However, if the landlord contests the claim with complex counter‑evidence, or if you feel uncomfortable appearing in court, you may consult a lawyer for advice or representation. Legal aid services (DLSA/NALSA) are also available at no cost.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self‑advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation or if the dispute escalates, consult a licensed advocate.

### LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE  
*(Security Deposit Refund – Unjust Rs 45,000 Deduction)*  

**Date:** 7 November 2026  

**Mode of Dispatch:** Speed Post – Acknowledgement Due (AD) / Registered Email (with read‑receipt)  

---

#### To,  

**Mr. Ramesh**  
[Landlord’s Address]  
Bengaluru – 5600XX  

---

#### Subject: **Demand for Refund of Unjustly Deducted Security Deposit (Rs 45,000) and Interest within 15 Days**  

---

### 1.  Under instructions from my client **[Tenant’s Full Name]** (hereinafter “the Tenant”), the undersigned hereby serves this legal notice as follows:  

---

### 2.  Facts of the Case  

| Sr. No. | Date / Period | Event |
|--------|---------------|-------|
| 1 | **Oct 2022 – Oct 2024** | The Tenant entered into a written lease for a 2‑BHK flat situated at HSR Layout, Bengaluru, for a period of two (2) years at a monthly rent of **Rs 28,000**. The Tenant paid a security deposit of **Rs 1,00,000** as per the lease. |
| 2 | **1 Oct 2024** | The Tenant served a one‑month notice (copy attached) to vacate the premises on or before **31 Oct 2024**. |
| 3 | **31 Oct 2024** | The Tenant vacated the flat, cleared all electricity & water dues, handed over the keys, and the landlord acknowledged receipt of the flat in **good condition** via WhatsApp (chat screenshot attached). |
| 4 | **Early Nov 2024 (within 3 days)** | The landlord promised to refund the entire security deposit through UPI within three days. |
| 5 | **Mid‑Nov 2024 (≈ 25 days after vacating)** | No refund was received; the landlord stopped answering calls. |
| 6 | **Mid‑Nov 2024 (yesterday)** | The landlord messaged that he is **deducting Rs 45,000** for repainting, marble polishing and deep cleaning, without any itemised bill or prior inspection. |

---

### 3.  Documents & Evidence in Possession (Annexure‑A)

1. Move‑in photographs of the flat.  
2. Move‑out hand‑over video.  
3. Bank statements showing monthly rent payments and the security‑deposit payment.  
4. WhatsApp chat where the landlord acknowledges receipt of the flat in good condition.  
5. Copy of the notice dated **1 Oct 2024**.  

*Documents yet to be produced (to be annexed if obtained):* signed lease agreement, receipt of security deposit, written notice of deduction, quotations/receipts for repainting, marble polishing or deep cleaning, UPI transaction history showing non‑receipt of refund.

---

### 4.  Legal Grounds  

| Provision | Act / Statute | Relevance |
|-----------|---------------|-----------|
| **Section 13** | Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (adopted by Karnataka) | Security deposit limited to two months’ rent and must be returned **within 30 days** of peaceful possession, after deducting only genuine, itemised charges. |
| **Section 14** | Model Tenancy Act, 2021 | No deduction is permissible for **normal wear and tear**; any deduction must be supported by an itemised bill. |
| **Section 21** | Model Tenancy Act, 2021 | Deposit disputes are to be adjudicated before the **Rent Authority / Rent Court**. |
| **Section 108(B)(m) & (q)** | Transfer of Property Act, 1882 | Tenant must keep the premises in as‑good‑as‑received condition; landlord must return the deposit after vacating. |
| **[unverified reference removed]** | Indian Contract Act, 1872 (for interest) | Entitles the creditor to **simple interest at 12 % per annum** for delayed payment. |
| **[unverified reference removed] & 74** | Specific Relief Act, 1963 (for damages) | Allows claim for **interest and compensation for loss** caused by breach of contract. |

The landlord’s unilateral deduction of **Rs 45,000** is **unjustified** because:

* The flat was handed back in **good condition** (as per video & WhatsApp acknowledgment).  
* No itemised bill or prior inspection was produced.  
* The deduction pertains to **normal wear and tear** (paint fading, routine cleaning) which is prohibited under Sec. 14 of the Model Tenancy Act.  

Hence, the landlord is **in breach of contract** and **statutory duty**.

---

### 5.  Demand  

In view of the above, the Tenant **hereby demands**:

1. **Refund of Rs 45,000** (the amount unjustly deducted).  
2. **Simple interest at 12 % per annum** from **31 Oct 2024** till the date of actual payment (interest calculated on a daily basis).  
3. **Compensation for litigation costs** (if any) and statutory damages as may be awarded by the Rent Authority / Small Causes Court.  

**All the above amounts are to be paid within **fifteen (15) days** of receipt of this notice**, i.e., **by 22 November 2026**.  

Payment may be made via UPI to **[Your UPI ID]** or by cheque in favour of **[Your Name]** payable at Bengaluru.

---

### 6.  Consequence of Non‑Compliance  

If the demanded amount is **not received** within the stipulated 15‑day period, the Tenant shall, **without any further notice**, proceed to:

* File a grievance before the **Karnataka Rent Authority** (or the appropriate Small Causes Court) under **Section 21** of the Model Tenancy Act, seeking:
  * Refund of the deducted amount with interest,
  * Statutory penalty for wrongful deduction,
  * Recovery of litigation costs and any other relief the forum deems fit.

* Claim **statutory interest at 12 % per annum** and **damages** as per Sections 73 & 74 of the Indian Contract Act and the Specific Relief Act.

The Tenant also reserves the right to approach the **Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum** if the landlord’s conduct amounts to unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

---

### 7.  Verification  

I, **[Tenant’s Full Name]**, the undersigned, do hereby **verify** that the contents of this notice are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief, and that no material fact has been concealed.

---

### 8.  Signature  

```
_____________________________  
[Tenant’s Full Name]  
Date: 7 Nov 2026
```

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Mr. Ramesh, as per Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act and the Model Tenancy framework, ordinary wear and tear like wall paint aging cannot be deducted from my deposit. I have the handover video and our chat proof. Please refund my balance 45,000 within 7 days.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Dekhiye, aapka reference Section 108 aur model tenancy ka hai, lekin hamare lease agreement mein clearly likha hai ki paint ki normal wear‑and‑tear ko bhi tenant ko replace karna hota hai, aur humare standard inspection report bhi ussi ko confirm karta hai. Humein aapka video aur chat mil gaya hai, lekin aapko bhi inspection report sign karni hoti thi jo aapne nahi ki. Phir bhi, hum aapki baat ko dhyan mein rakhte hue, Rs 45,000 ka deduction thoda kam kar dete hain – Rs 30,000 hi rakhte hain, aur aapko 7 din ke andar baaki refund kar denge. Agar aapko ismein koi problem hai, to aap legal notice bhej sakte hain, tab hum aage ki baat karenge.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You cited a specific statutory provision (Section 108) and backed it up with concrete evidence (handover video, chat logs), which forces the landlord to acknowledge the claim.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Mention the exact clause in your lease that limits deductions for wear‑and‑tear, and reference the applicable state rent control act or RERA provisions that mandate full deposit return within a specific period, plus interest for delay.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Ask for the signed inspection report and demand the full Rs 45,000 plus statutory interest, citing the lease clause and RERA/State Rent Act.
